title: Lucida FAQ: pricing, FSRS, AI cards, import and more
description: Short answers about Lucida: what’s free, what Pro adds, how FSRS spaced repetition works, AI-made cards, Learn mode, live games, import and export.
lead: Short answers to the questions people ask most about Lucida, from pricing and spaced repetition to AI-made cards, importing, sharing and live games. If yours isn’t here, email team@lucida.cards.

bullets: [Spaced repetition with FSRS](/features/spaced-repetition): how every review is planned
[AI flashcards](/features/ai-flashcards): connect Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor and ask for cards
[Learn mode](/features/learn-mode): quizzes on your own cards
[Shared decks](/features/shared-decks), [classes](/features/classes) and [live games](/features/live-games): study with other people
Made for [students](/for/students), [medical students](/for/med-school), [the MCAT](/for/mcat), [language learners](/for/language-learning) and [teachers](/for/teachers)

faq.q: What is Lucida?
faq.a: Lucida is a flashcard app that runs in your browser. Your own AI (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any app that supports MCP) can make your cards through a personal link, and FSRS spaced repetition plans every review.

faq.q: Is Lucida free?
faq.a: Yes. Unlimited decks and cards, spaced repetition, Learn mode, sharing, live games, classes, up to 100 pictures and sounds, and import and export are free. Pro is optional.

faq.q: How much does Lucida Pro cost, and what does it add?
faq.a: Pro is $5.99 a month or $49.99 a year (as of September 2026). It adds exam dates, stats on what you’re weak at, unlimited pictures and sounds, themes, the hardest cards on decks you share, photo covers, natural voices for sound cards, more AI explanations, and tuning the schedule to your own reviews.

faq.q: Do I need an account?
faq.a: To make and study decks, yes. You sign in with an email code, Google or Apple. You don’t need an account to join a live game or to read a shared deck’s page.

faq.q: Is there an iPhone or Android app?
faq.a: Not yet. Lucida is a web app that works in the browser on phones, tablets and computers, including iPhone and Android. A native iPhone app is being built and isn’t on the App Store yet.

faq.q: Does Lucida work offline?
faq.a: No. Lucida needs an internet connection.

faq.q: How old do I need to be to use Lucida?
faq.a: 13. Lucida’s terms require it, and its privacy policy says it isn’t meant for children under 13.

faq.q: Who can see my cards?
faq.a: Only you, unless you share a deck, add it to a class or play it in a live game. An AI app can see them only if you connect it with your personal link, and only as far as you allow on the Connect AI page.

faq.q: Does Lucida use my cards to train AI?
faq.a: No. Lucida’s privacy policy says it doesn’t sell your data, use it for ads, or use your cards to train AI models. What you share with an AI app is covered by that company’s own policy.

faq.q: How do I contact Lucida?
faq.a: Email team@lucida.cards.

faq.q: What is spaced repetition?
faq.a: Spaced repetition is reviewing something again after a gap that grows each time you remember it, so you see it just before you’d forget it. Lucida uses it to choose which cards to show each day.

faq.q: What is FSRS, and which version does Lucida use?
faq.a: FSRS (Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler) is an open-source algorithm that estimates how likely you are to remember each card and schedules the next review for when that chance reaches your goal. Lucida uses FSRS version 5. See [spaced repetition](/features/spaced-repetition).

faq.q: What does the Remember goal do?
faq.a: It’s the chance you want of remembering a card when it comes back. The default is 90%, and each deck can go from 70 to 97%. Higher goals mean shorter gaps and more reviews a day.

faq.q: How many new cards should I study a day?
faq.a: Lucida starts at 20. Each new card adds reviews later, so if your due list keeps growing, lower the number. Anki’s manual estimates that 20 new cards a day settles at roughly 200 reviews a day.

faq.q: What happens if I miss a day or a week?
faq.a: Nothing resets. FSRS uses the real time since each review, so you just start on the list. If a lot is overdue, pause new cards until you catch up.

faq.q: Can I turn spaced repetition off?
faq.a: Yes. Turn off Schedule with FSRS in Settings or for one deck, or grade with piles, which only sort cards. With it off, cards don’t get a next review date.

faq.q: What is a leech?
faq.a: A card you keep forgetting. Lucida tags a card Leech after 8 forgets so you can find it and fix it. On Pro you can change the count, or pause such cards.

faq.q: Can I set an exam date?
faq.a: Yes, on Pro. From 30 days before the exam, cards you’d probably forget by then come up early, and Stats shows how much of the deck you’d likely remember on the day.

faq.q: Can Lucida tune the schedule to my own reviews?
faq.a: Yes, on Pro, once you have 400 graded reviews (at least 100 of them on cards you’d already learned). It runs in your browser, and you can switch back to the standard settings at any time.

faq.q: What kinds of cards can I make?
faq.a: Four: question and answer, fill in the blank, picture (with optional hidden parts) and sound.

faq.q: How do I make a fill-in-the-blank card?
faq.a: Add a Blank card and put double brackets around the words to hide, like “The [[mitochondrion]] makes ATP.” Each blank becomes its own card, or you can choose one card for all of them.

faq.q: Can I use bold, lists or math on cards?
faq.a: Yes: bold, italics, underline, strikethrough, highlights, headings, bullet and numbered lists, and simple math like powers, subscripts, fractions, roots and Greek letters. It doesn’t do full equation layout.

faq.q: Can I add pictures and sounds?
faq.a: Yes. Free includes up to 100 cards with a picture or a sound, and Pro has no 100 limit. You can record yourself, upload a file (up to 4 MB), or have your device read words aloud.

faq.q: What is image occlusion?
faq.a: It hides parts of a picture behind boxes, so you recall what’s under each one. Each box becomes its own card. It’s free, with up to 30 boxes on a picture. See [image occlusion](/features/image-occlusion).

faq.q: How do I organize my decks?
faq.a: Put decks in folders (one level), tag cards by topic, drag decks and cards to reorder them, and use the All cards view to search and filter.

faq.q: How do I make flashcards with ChatGPT or Claude?
faq.a: Copy your personal link from Connect AI, add it to your AI app (as a custom connector in Claude, or a developer-mode app in ChatGPT), then ask for cards. The cards land in your decks. See [AI flashcards](/features/ai-flashcards).

faq.q: Which AI apps work with Lucida?
faq.a: Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor have steps in Lucida, and any app that can add a remote MCP server by its web address can use your link. Gemini and Grok can add custom MCP servers too, but Lucida has no steps for them.

faq.q: Do I need a paid AI subscription?
faq.a: Not for Lucida itself: you can type cards, import them or study shared decks with no AI. Claude’s free plan allows one custom connector, and OpenAI lists ChatGPT’s developer mode for Pro, Plus, Business, Enterprise and Education accounts.

faq.q: Can the AI delete my cards?
faq.a: Only if you switch on Delete cards on the Connect AI page, and it’s off by default. You can also turn on Let me check AI cards first, so new cards and changes wait for your OK.

faq.q: Are AI-made flashcards accurate?
faq.a: Not always. Lucida’s terms say AI apps can make mistakes and to check what matters, especially before an exam. Give your AI your own notes and read the cards.

faq.q: Does Lucida have its own AI?
faq.a: Only for Explain, a short explanation of why a card’s answer is right: 3 a day on Free and up to 200 a day on Pro. Making cards and quizzes uses your own AI app.

faq.q: What is Learn mode, and is it free?
faq.a: Learn mode quizzes you on your cards with multiple choice, true or false, matching, fill-in-the-blank and typed questions until you’ve got each one right twice in a row. It’s free. See [Learn mode](/features/learn-mode).

faq.q: How do live games work?
faq.a: You open a room from a deck on a computer, and players join on their phones with a 6-digit code and a name. Everyone answers the same questions for points, and a leaderboard and podium follow. A room holds up to 60 players. See [live games](/features/live-games).

faq.q: Do players need an account for a live game?
faq.a: No. They need only the code and a name. The host needs a Lucida account.

faq.q: How do I share a deck?
faq.a: Open the deck’s settings, choose Sharing, and pick Private, Link only or Public. Send the link, or let people find a public deck in Discover. See [shared decks](/features/shared-decks).

faq.q: What’s the difference between studying a deck and making a copy?
faq.a: Studying follows the owner’s changes, and you can’t edit the cards, but you can suggest changes. A copy is your own deck to change, and it can offer you the owner’s later changes to take or skip.

faq.q: How do classes work?
faq.a: A teacher makes a class and gets a six-letter code and an invite link. They add decks, assign them with a due date, and see progress that students choose to share. Teachers never see individual answers. See [classes](/features/classes).

faq.q: Can I import my cards from Anki?
faq.a: Yes, through Anki’s Notes in Plain Text export, not the .apkg file. Scheduling, pictures, sounds and tags don’t come along. See [importing](/features/import).

faq.q: Can I import my Quizlet sets?
faq.a: Yes. On quizlet.com, open a set you made, choose Export, then Copy text, and paste it into Lucida’s Import cards. Quizlet doesn’t export pictures.

faq.q: Can I export my cards?
faq.a: Yes, on any plan. Export one deck as a CSV file, or everything (decks, cards and review history) as one lucida.json file from Settings.

faq.q: How do I delete my data or my account?
faq.a: In Settings, Delete account removes every deck, card and review, and your profile and shared decks. To remove your email address too, write to team@lucida.cards. Lucida’s privacy policy says it does this within 30 days.

faq.q: Can I cancel Pro, and what happens to my cards?
faq.a: Yes, from Settings. Pro stays on until the end of the time you paid for. Every deck and card stays yours, and only the Pro extras switch off.

faq.q: Is there a student discount?
faq.a: The pricing page lists none. There’s a free plan, and Pro at $5.99 a month or $49.99 a year (as of September 2026).

faq.q: What counts toward the 100 pictures and sounds?
faq.a: Each picture or sound on a card. Text cards never count. A picture with hidden parts counts once, a sound card that uses your device’s voice stores no file so it doesn’t count, and neither do pictures and sounds in decks other people share with you.
